31	@HiltViewModel
32	class ExploreViewModel @Inject constructor(
33	    private val repository: HackersPubRepository
34	) : ViewModel() {
35	
36	    private val _uiState = MutableStateFlow(ExploreUiState())
37	    val uiState: StateFlow<ExploreUiState> = _uiState.asStateFlow()
38	
39	    private var lastLoadTime: Instant? = null
40	    private val staleThresholdSeconds = 60L
41	
42	    init {
43	        loadTimeline()
44	    }
45	
46	    fun refreshIfStale() {
47	        val last = lastLoadTime ?: return
48	        if (Instant.now().epochSecond - last.epochSecond > staleThresholdSeconds) {
49	            refresh()
50	        }
51	    }
52	
53	    fun selectTab(tab: ExploreTab) {
54	        if (tab != _uiState.value.selectedTab) {
55	            _uiState.update {
56	                it.copy(
57	                    selectedTab = tab,
58	                    posts = emptyList(),
59	                    endCursor = null,
60	                    hasNextPage = false
61	                )
62	            }
63	            loadTimeline()
64	        }
65	    }
66	
67	    private fun loadTimeline() {
68	        viewModelScope.launch {
69	            _uiState.update { it.copy(isLoading = true, error = null) }
70	
71	            val result = when (_uiState.value.selectedTab) {
72	                ExploreTab.LOCAL -> repository.getLocalTimeline(refresh = true)
73	                ExploreTab.GLOBAL -> repository.getPublicTimeline(refresh = true)
74	            }
75	
76	            result
77	                .onSuccess { data ->
78	                    lastLoadTime = Instant.now()
79	                    _uiState.update {
80	                        it.copy(
81	                            posts = data.posts,
82	                            hasNextPage = data.hasNextPage,
83	                            endCursor = data.endCursor,
84	                            isLoading = false
85	                        )
86	                    }
87	                }
88	                .onFailure { error ->
89	                    _uiState.update {
90	                        it.copy(
91	                            error = error.message,
92	                            isLoading = false
93	                        )
94	                    }
95	                }
96	        }
97	    }
98	
99	    fun refresh() {
100	        viewModelScope.launch {
101	            _uiState.update { it.copy(isRefreshing = true, error = null) }
102	
103	            val result = when (_uiState.value.selectedTab) {
104	                ExploreTab.LOCAL -> repository.getLocalTimeline(refresh = true)
105	                ExploreTab.GLOBAL -> repository.getPublicTimeline(refresh = true)
106	            }
107	
108	            result
109	                .onSuccess { data ->
110	                    lastLoadTime = Instant.now()
111	                    _uiState.update {
112	                        it.copy(
113	                            posts = data.posts,
114	                            hasNextPage = data.hasNextPage,
115	                            endCursor = data.endCursor,
116	                            isRefreshing = false
117	                        )
118	                    }
119	                }
120	                .onFailure { error ->
121	                    _uiState.update {
122	                        it.copy(
123	                            error = error.message,
124	                            isRefreshing = false
125	                        )
126	                    }
127	                }
128	        }
129	    }
130	
131	    fun loadMore() {
132	        val currentState = _uiState.value
133	        if (!currentState.hasNextPage || currentState.isLoadingMore) return
134	
135	        viewModelScope.launch {
136	            _uiState.update { it.copy(isLoadingMore = true) }
137	
138	            val result = when (currentState.selectedTab) {
139	                ExploreTab.LOCAL -> repository.getLocalTimeline(after = currentState.endCursor)
140	                ExploreTab.GLOBAL -> repository.getPublicTimeline(after = currentState.endCursor)
141	            }
142	
143	            result
144	                .onSuccess { data ->
145	                    _uiState.update {
146	                        it.copy(
147	                            posts = it.posts + data.posts,
148	                            hasNextPage = data.hasNextPage,
149	                            endCursor = data.endCursor,
150	                            isLoadingMore = false
151	                        )
152	                    }
153	                }
154	                .onFailure {
155	                    _uiState.update { it.copy(isLoadingMore = false) }
156	                }
157	        }
158	    }
159	
160	    fun sharePost(postId: String) {
161	        viewModelScope.launch {
162	            repository.sharePost(postId)
163	                .onSuccess {
164	                    _uiState.update { state ->
165	                        state.copy(
166	                            posts = state.posts.map { post ->
167	                                if (post.id == postId) {
168	                                    post.copy(
169	                                        viewerHasShared = true,
170	                                        engagementStats = post.engagementStats.copy(
171	                                            shares = post.engagementStats.shares + 1
172	                                        )
173	                                    )
174	                                } else post
175	                            }
176	                        )
177	                    }
178	                }
179	        }
180	    }
181	
182	    fun unsharePost(postId: String) {
183	        viewModelScope.launch {
184	            repository.unsharePost(postId)
185	                .onSuccess {
186	                    _uiState.update { state ->
187	                        state.copy(
188	                            posts = state.posts.map { post ->
189	                                if (post.id == postId) {
190	                                    post.copy(
191	                                        viewerHasShared = false,
192	                                        engagementStats = post.engagementStats.copy(

194	                                        )
195	                                    )
196	                                } else post
197	                            }
198	                        )
199	                    }
200	                }
201	        }

)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}"

237	                } else group

Yes — you can use `fswatch` (macOS) or `entr`:

**With `entr`:**
```bash
find app/src -name '*.kt' -o -name '*.xml' | entr -s './gradlew installDebug'
```

**With `fswatch`:**
```bash
fswatch -o app/src | xargs -n1 -I{} ./gradlew installDebug
```

Install with `brew install entr` or `brew install fswatch`.

`entr` is simpler — it re-runs the command whenever any matched file changes. Add `-r` to restart if the build is still running when a new change comes in:

```bash
find app/src -name '*.kt' -o -name '*.xml' | entr -rs './gradlew installDebug'
```

> DEVELOPER

Hmmm, How about hotmodulereloading for android kotlin jetpack compose?

> AGENT

Jetpack Compose has **Live Edit** built into Android Studio — it pushes code changes to the running app without a full rebuild. It works for composable function body changes (not signature changes or non-composable code).

Enable it in Android Studio: **Settings → Editor → Live Edit** → check "Push edits manually" or "Push edits automatically".

There's no equivalent for CLI-only workflows though. Outside Android Studio, the fastest option is `./gradlew installDebug` with Gradle's build cache (incremental builds are usually fast after the first one).

If you're not using Android Studio, the `entr` approach is your best bet for a CLI watch-and-deploy loop.

- `<ruby>漢字<rp>(</rp><rt>かんじ</rt><rp>)</rp></ruby>` renders with the base text normally and the furigana as small superscript text
- `<rp>` content (fallback parentheses) is hidden
- `<rt>` content rendered at 0.6x font size with superscript baseline shift

> AGENT

Found the issue. `MediaImage` wraps `AsyncImage` inside a `Box` — but the `modifier` is applied to `AsyncImage`, **not** to the outer `Box`. So `weight(1f)` and `height()` are on the `AsyncImage` inside an unconstrained `Box`. The `Box` itself has no size constraints.

I need to move the modifier to the `Box`.

> TOOL

tool_use Edit

> AGENT

That was the root cause. The `modifier` (with `weight()`, `height()`, `clip()`) was being applied to `AsyncImage` inside an unconstrained `Box`, so layout constraints like `weight(1f)` were ignored. Now the modifier is on the `Box` itself, and `AsyncImage` fills it with `fillMaxSize()`. This should fix all grid layouts — 2, 3, and 4+ images.

> AGENT

No `fetchPolicy` is set, so Apollo uses the default which is cache-first with the normalized cache. The timeline query fetches the post with `engagementStats.replies = 0` (at that point there may be no replies), and the cache stores it. When PostDetail later loads, it hits the cache and gets the stale `replies: 0` count.

The fix: force a network fetch for PostDetail.

The issue was Apollo's normalized cache returning stale data. The timeline loads a post with `replies: 0`, caches it, and when PostDetail loads the same post, it hits the cache instead of fetching fresh data from the network. Now `PostDetailQuery` always fetches from the network (`FetchPolicy.NetworkOnly`), so reply counts and actual replies will be up to date.

  "old_string": "@Composable\nfun MediaImage(\n    url: String,\n    alt: String?,\n    modifier: Modifier = Modifier\n) {\n    val colors = LocalAppColors.current\n    var showPreview by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }\n\n    Box(modifier = modifier) {\n        AsyncImage(\n            model = url,\n            contentDescription = alt,\n            modifier = Modifier\n                .fillMaxSize()\n                .border(\n                    width = 1.dp,\n                    color = colors.divider,\n                    shape = RoundedCornerShape(AppShapes.mediaRadius)\n                )\n                .clickable { showPreview = true },\n            contentScale = ContentScale.Crop\n        )\n    }\n\n    if (showPreview) {\n        MediaPreviewDialog(\n            url = url,\n            alt = alt,\n            onDismiss = { showPreview = false }\n        )\n    }\n}",
  "new_string": "@Composable\nfun MediaImage(\n    url: String,\n    alt: String?,\n    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,\n    isVideo: Boolean = false,\n    thumbnailUrl: String? = null\n) {\n    val colors = LocalAppColors.current\n    val context = LocalContext.current\n    var showPreview by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }\n\n    Box(modifier = modifier) {\n        AsyncImage(\n            model = if (isVideo) (thumbnailUrl ?: url) else url,\n            contentDescription = alt,\n            modifier = Modifier\n                .fillMaxSize()\n                .border(\n                    width = 1.dp,\n                    color = colors.divider,\n                    shape = RoundedCornerShape(AppShapes.mediaRadius)\n                )\n                .clickable {\n                    if (isVideo) {\n                        val intent = Intent(Intent.ACTION_VIEW, Uri.parse(url))\n                        intent.setDataAndType(Uri.parse(url), \"video/*\")\n                        context.startActivity(intent)\n                    } else {\n                        showPreview = true\n                    }\n                },\n            contentScale = ContentScale.Crop\n        )\n\n        if (isVideo) {\n            Box(\n                contentAlignment = Alignment.Center,\n                modifier = Modifier\n                    .fillMaxSize()\n                    .background(Color.Black.copy(alpha = 0.3f))\n            ) {\n                Icon(\n                    imageVector = Icons.Default.PlayArrow,\n                    contentDescription = \"Play video\",\n                    tint = Color.White,\n                    modifier = Modifier.size(48.dp)\n                )\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    if (showPreview) {\n        MediaPreviewDialog(\n            url = url,\n            alt = alt,\n            onDismiss = { showPreview = false }\n        )\n    }\n}"
}

> AGENT

It's using `hackerspub://verify` — the custom scheme. This should open the app directly when tapped in email, since custom schemes bypass the browser.

If it's still not working, the issue is likely that the email client doesn't render `hackerspub://` as a clickable link (we discussed this earlier — email clients only hyperlink `http://` and `https://` URLs).

Two options:

1. **Server-side fix**: Disable Mailgun click tracking so `https://hackers.pub/sign/in/...` links go directly to the app (needs `assetlinks.json` + `autoVerify`)

2. **Hybrid approach**: Use `https://hackers.pub/sign/in/{token}?code={code}` in the email, and add a redirect on the web server at `/sign/in/[token]` that detects mobile and redirects to `hackerspub://verify?token=...&code=...`

Which approach would you prefer? Or is there a different issue you're seeing?

> DEVELOPER

Okay, If already autoVerify is setup, and updating assetlink solve this issue? Or Do I need to update assetlink and rebuild app?

> AGENT

No rebuild needed. `autoVerify` is already in the manifest from our earlier changes. You just need to:

1. Deploy `assetlinks.json` to `https://hackers.pub/.well-known/assetlinks.json` (we already created it in `web-next/public/.well-known/`)
2. On the device, clear the app's link verification state and re-verify:

```bash
adb shell pm set-app-links --package pub.hackers.android.dev 2 all
```

Or uninstall and reinstall the app — Android checks `assetlinks.json` on install.

The key thing: make sure the `package_name` and `sha256_cert_fingerprints` in `assetlinks.json` match your installed app's signing key. The current file has `pub.hackers.app` — if your debug build uses `pub.hackers.android.dev`, you'll need to update it.

> AGENT

The intent filters are there. The issue is likely that Mailgun's click tracking redirect wraps the URL before it reaches the device. Even with `autoVerify` and `assetlinks.json`, the browser handles the Mailgun redirect URL (e.g., `https://email.hackers.pub/...`), and when it resolves to `https://hackers.pub/sign/in/...`, the redirect happens **inside** the browser, so Android never gets a chance to intercept it.

The fix: change the email to use `https://hackers.pub/sign/in/...` directly (no Mailgun tracking), OR disable Mailgun click tracking.

Can you check — is the link in the email `https://hackers.pub/sign/in/...` directly, or does it go through a tracking redirect like `https://email.hackers.pub/...` or `https://clicks.mailgun.net/...`?

You can long-press the link in the email to see the actual URL.

For local testing, force it:

```bash
adb shell pm set-app-links --package pub.hackers.android.dev 2 all
```

Or if you want the debug build to also verify properly, the `assetlinks.json` needs both entries. Want me to add it?

> DEVELOPER

Okay, it worked

> AGENT

So the app handles the deep link correctly. The problem is the **email client** — it opens links in its own embedded webview instead of passing them to the Android system, so App Links never get a chance to intercept.

This is a common issue with Gmail, Outlook, etc. — they have built-in browsers. Unfortunately there's no fix from the app side.

The workaround: go back to using `hackerspub://verify` custom scheme for the email. Custom schemes can't be opened in a webview, so the email client is forced to hand them off to the app. The downside (link not clickable in some clients) is better than the link opening in a webview.

Or — add a "Open in app" button on the web page at `/sign/in/[token]`. When the user lands there in the email client's webview, they tap the button which redirects to `hackerspub://verify?token=...&code=...`. This is the most reliable approach and works with any email client.

Want me to keep it as `hackerspub://verify` for now?

> DEVELOPER

Is that the best?????

> AGENT

No. The best approach is the **"Open in app" button on the web page**.

The flow:
1. Email sends `https://hackers.pub/sign/in/<token>?code=<code>` (clickable in all email clients)
2. User taps → email client opens it in webview → web page loads
3. Web page detects mobile and shows an "Open in app" button linking to `hackerspub://verify?token=...&code=...`
4. User taps → app opens directly

This works with every email client, every redirect, no assetlinks dependency. It's what most apps do (Slack, Discord, etc.).

But this requires a change to the **web project's** `/sign/in/[token]` page — not the Android app. Want me to add that to the hackerspub web project?

Instead of webview, i want to give option or force open the macthed app

> AGENT

The best way: use Android's `intent://` URI on the web page. It forces the system to open the app if installed, with no webview interference.

# Passkey Authentication for hackerspub-android

## Context

HackersPub server already has full passkey (WebAuthn/FIDO2) support via `@simplewebauthn/server`. The Android app needs to integrate with the existing GraphQL API using Android's Credential Manager API.

## Server-Side API (already implemented)

### Authentication (login)
- `getPasskeyAuthenticationOptions(sessionId: UUID)` → returns `PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON`
- `loginByPasskey(sessionId: UUID, authenticationResponse: JSON)` → returns `Session`

### Registration (add new passkey, requires auth)
- `getPasskeyRegistrationOptions(accountId: GlobalID)` → returns `PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON`
- `verifyPasskeyRegistration(accountId: GlobalID, name: String, registrationResponse: JSON)` → returns `PasskeyRegistrationResult`

### Management (requires auth)
- `revokePasskey(passkeyId: GlobalID)` → returns `ID`
- `account.passkeys` → connection of registered passkeys

### Key server details
- RP ID: `new URL(origin).hostname` (e.g., `hackers.pub`)
- RP Name: `"Hackers' Pub"`
- Uses `@simplewebauthn/server` for challenge generation and verification
- Authentication options stored in KV with 5-minute TTL

## Android Implementation Plan

### Prerequisites
- **assetlinks.json**: Must be hosted at `https://hackers.pub/.well-known/assetlinks.json` with:
  ```json
  [{
    "relation": ["delegate_permission/common.handle_all_urls",
                 "delegate_permission/common.get_login_creds"],
    "target": {
      "namespace": "android_app",
      "package_name": "pub.hackers.app",
      "sha256_cert_fingerprints": ["<signing-cert-sha256>"]
    }
  }]
  ```
  The `common.get_login_creds` relation is required for passkey access.

### Dependencies
```kotlin
implementation("androidx.credentials:credentials:1.3.0")
implementation("androidx.credentials:credentials-play-services-auth:1.3.0")
```

### Authentication Flow (login with passkey)
1. Generate a temporary `sessionId` (UUID)
2. Call `getPasskeyAuthenticationOptions(sessionId)` GraphQL mutation to get WebAuthn challenge
3. Create `GetPublicKeyCredentialOption` with the options JSON
4. Call `CredentialManager.getCredential()` to prompt the user
5. Send the credential response via `loginByPasskey(sessionId, authenticationResponse)` GraphQL mutation
6. Store the returned session token

### Registration Flow (add passkey to account, post-login)
1. Call `getPasskeyRegistrationOptions(accountId)` to get challenge
2. Create `CreatePublicKeyCredentialRequest` with the options JSON
3. Call `CredentialManager.createCredential()` to create key pair
4. Send response via `verifyPasskeyRegistration(accountId, name, registrationResponse)`

### Passkey Management (settings screen)
- List passkeys via `account.passkeys` connection
- Revoke passkeys via `revokePasskey(passkeyId)`

## Reference Files

### Server
- `models/passkey.ts` — Core WebAuthn logic (registration options, verification, authentication)
- `graphql/passkey.ts` — GraphQL mutations for registration/revocation, Passkey type
- `graphql/login.ts` — GraphQL mutations for authentication (`getPasskeyAuthenticationOptions`, `loginByPasskey`)
- `web/islands/SignForm.tsx` — Reference client implementation (browser-based)

### Android
- Current project: `/Users/kodingwarrior/fediverse/hackerspub-android`

mutation LoginByUsername($username: String!, $locale: Locale!, $verifyUrl: URITemplate!) {
    loginByUsername(username: $username, locale: $locale, verifyUrl: $verifyUrl) {
        ... on LoginChallenge {
            token
        }
        ... on AccountNotFoundError {
            query
        }
    }
}
```
- Returns `LoginChallenge` with `token` or `AccountNotFoundError`

}

## Passkey GraphQL API Specification Report

Based on my exploration of the hackerspub server project, here's the complete passkey GraphQL API mapping:

### 1. **Login (Authentication) Mutations**

#### `getPasskeyAuthenticationOptions` (Mutation)
**File:** `/Users/kodingwarrior/fediverse/hackerspub/graphql/login.ts` (lines 270-287)

**GraphQL Definition:**
```graphql
getPasskeyAuthenticationOptions(sessionId: UUID!): JSON!
```

**Input:**
- `sessionId: UUID!` - Temporary session ID for passkey authentication

**Output:**
- `JSON` - Returns `PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON` object containing:
  - `challenge: string` (base64-encoded)
  - `timeout: number`
  - `rpId: string`
  - `userVerification: string`
  - `allowCredentials: Array` (empty for first-time auth)

**Implementation:** Calls `getAuthenticationOptions(ctx.kv, ctx.fedCtx.canonicalOrigin, args.sessionId)`

---

#### `loginByPasskey` (Mutation)
**File:** `/Users/kodingwarrior/fediverse/hackerspub/graphql/login.ts` (lines 289-325)

**GraphQL Definition:**
```graphql
loginByPasskey(
  sessionId: UUID!
  authenticationResponse: JSON!
): Session
```

**Input Parameters:**
- `sessionId: UUID!` - Temporary session ID (must match getPasskeyAuthenticationOptions call)
- `authenticationResponse: JSON!` - WebAuthn `AuthenticationResponseJSON` containing:
  - `id: string` - Credential ID
  - `rawId: string` - Base64url-encoded credential ID
  - `response: { clientDataJSON: string, authenticatorData: string, signature: string }`
  - `type: "public-key"`

**Output:**
- `Session` (nullable) - If authentication succeeds:
  ```graphql
  type Session {
    id: UUID!
  }
  ```

**Response:** Returns session object with ID on success, `null` on failure

---

### 2. **Registration Mutations**

#### `getPasskeyRegistrationOptions` (Mutation)
**File:** `/Users/kodingwarrior/fediverse/hackerspub/graphql/passkey.ts` (lines 90-113)

**GraphQL Definition:**
```graphql
getPasskeyRegistrationOptions(accountId: ID!): JSON!
```

**Input:**
- `accountId: ID!` - Global ID of the account (requires authentication)

**Output:**
- `JSON` - Returns `PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON` containing:
  - `challenge: string` (base64-encoded)
  - `rp: { name: string, id: string }` - Relying Party info ("Hackers' Pub", domain hostname)
  - `user: { id: string, name: string, displayName: string }`
  - `pubKeyCredParams: Array<{ type: "public-key", alg: number }>`
  - `timeout: number`
  - `attestation: "none"`
  - `excludeCredentials: Array` - Existing passkeys for this account

**Implementation:** Calls `getRegistrationOptions(ctx.kv, ctx.fedCtx.canonicalOrigin, account)` from models/passkey.ts

---

#### `verifyPasskeyRegistration` (Mutation)
**File:** `/Users/kodingwarrior/fediverse/hackerspub/graphql/passkey.ts` (lines 114-156)

**GraphQL Definition:**
```graphql
verifyPasskeyRegistration(
  accountId: ID!
  name: String!
  registrationResponse: JSON!
): PasskeyRegistrationResult!
```

**Input Parameters:**
- `accountId: ID!` - Global ID of account (requires authentication)
- `name: String!` - User-provided name for the passkey (e.g., "My iPhone")
- `registrationResponse: JSON!` - WebAuthn `RegistrationResponseJSON`:
  - `id: string` - New credential ID
  - `rawId: string` - Base64url-encoded ID
  - `response: { clientDataJSON: string, attestationObject: string }`
  - `type: "public-key"`

**Output:**
```graphql
type PasskeyRegistrationResult {
  verified: Boolean!
  passkey: Passkey
}

type Passkey implements Node {
  id: ID!
  name: String!
  created: DateTime!
  lastUsed: DateTime
}
```

**Response Example:**
```json
{
  "verified": true,
  "passkey": {
    "id": "base64-encoded-credential-id",
    "name": "My iPhone",
    "created": "2024-04-10T15:30:00Z",
    "lastUsed": null
  }
}
```

#### `revokePasskey` (Mutation)
**File:** `/Users/kodingwarrior/fediverse/hackerspub/graphql/passkey.ts` (lines 157-178)

**GraphQL Definition:**
```graphql
revokePasskey(passkeyId: ID!): ID
```

**Input:**
- `passkeyId: ID!` - Global ID of the passkey to revoke

**Output:**
- `ID` (nullable) - Returns the encoded global ID of the revoked passkey on success, `null` on failure

---

### 3. **Web Client Implementation Patterns**

**File:** `/Users/kodingwarrior/fediverse/hackerspub/web-next/src/routes/(root)/sign/index.tsx` (lines 86-98)

**Login Flow:**
```typescript
// 1. Get options
const optionsResponse = await fetch(mutation with sessionId);
const options = optionsResponse.getPasskeyAuthenticationOptions;

// 2. Call WebAuthn
const authenticationResponse = await startAuthentication({
  optionsJSON: options as PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON,
  useBrowserAutofill: false // for manual trigger
});

// 3. Verify and create session
const loginResponse = await fetch(mutation with sessionId, authenticationResponse);
if (loginResponse.loginByPasskey?.id) {
  setSessionCookie(loginResponse.loginByPasskey.id);
}
```

**Registration Flow (from `/Users/kodingwarrior/fediverse/hackerspub/web-next/src/routes/(root)/[handle]/settings/passkeys.tsx` lines 216-292):**
```typescript
// 1. Get registration options
const optionsResponse = await getOptions({ accountId: account.id });
const options = optionsResponse.getPasskeyRegistrationOptions;

// 2. Call WebAuthn registration
const registrationResponse = await startRegistration({
  optionsJSON: options as PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON,
});

// 3. Verify registration
const verifyResponse = await verifyRegistration({
  accountId: account.id,
  name: passkeyName,
  registrationResponse,
  connections: [connectionId],
});

if (verifyResponse.verifyPasskeyRegistration.verified) {
  // Success - passkey is ready to use
}
```

---

### 4. **Type Signatures Summary**

**Input/Output JSON Types (from @simplewebauthn/server):**

| Type | Use | Key Fields |
|------|-----|-----------|
| `PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON` | getPasskeyAuthenticationOptions response | `challenge`, `rpId`, `userVerification`, `allowCredentials` |
| `AuthenticationResponseJSON` | loginByPasskey input | `id`, `rawId`, `response.clientDataJSON`, `response.authenticatorData`, `response.signature` |
| `PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON` | getPasskeyRegistrationOptions response | `challenge`, `rp`, `user`, `pubKeyCredParams`, `excludeCredentials` |
| `RegistrationResponseJSON` | verifyPasskeyRegistration input | `id`, `rawId`, `response.clientDataJSON`, `response.attestationObject` |

---

### 5. **Key Constants**

**From `/Users/kodingwarrior/fediverse/hackerspub/models/passkey.ts`:**
- `RP_NAME` = "Hackers' Pub"
- `KV_NAMESPACE` = "passkey"
- Authentication options timeout: 5 minutes (300 seconds)
- Attestation type: "none"

---

### 6. **Error Handling**

- `getPasskeyAuthenticationOptions`: Requires valid sessionId (generated client-side as UUID)
- `loginByPasskey`: Returns `null` if verification fails
- `getPasskeyRegistrationOptions`: Requires authentication (session)
- `verifyPasskeyRegistration`: Returns `verified: false` if verification fails
- `revokePasskey`: Returns `null` if passkey doesn't exist or not authorized

---

This API is built on **@simplewebauthn/server** for cryptographic operations and uses **Drizzle ORM** for database persistence. The passkey table stores: `id`, `accountId`, `name`, `publicKey`, `webauthnUserId`, `counter`, `deviceType`, `backedUp`, `transports`, `created`, `lastUsed`.

## Approved Plan:
# Plan: Passkey (WebAuthn/FIDO2) Authentication

## Context

The HackersPub server already has full passkey support. The Android app currently only supports username + email verification code login. Adding passkey support enables biometric/PIN login (fingerprint, face unlock) without email codes, and lets users register new passkeys from the app.

## Step 1: Add Dependencies

**File:** `app/build.gradle.kts`

Add Credential Manager libraries:
```kotlin
implementation("androidx.credentials:credentials:1.5.0-rc01")
implementation("androidx.credentials:credentials-play-services-auth:1.5.0-rc01")
```

## Step 2: Add GraphQL Operations

**File:** `app/src/main/graphql/pub/hackers/android/operations.graphql`

Add 4 mutations:
```graphql
mutation GetPasskeyAuthenticationOptions($sessionId: UUID!) {
    getPasskeyAuthenticationOptions(sessionId: $sessionId)
}

mutation LoginByPasskey($sessionId: UUID!, $authenticationResponse: JSON!) {
    loginByPasskey(sessionId: $sessionId, authenticationResponse: $authenticationResponse) {
        id
        account { id username name avatarUrl handle }
    }
}

mutation GetPasskeyRegistrationOptions($accountId: ID!) {
    getPasskeyRegistrationOptions(accountId: $accountId)
}

mutation VerifyPasskeyRegistration($accountId: ID!, $name: String!, $registrationResponse: JSON!) {
    verifyPasskeyRegistration(accountId: $accountId, name: $name, registrationResponse: $registrationResponse) {
        verified
        passkey { id name created lastUsed }
    }
}
```

Also add a query for listing passkeys and a mutation for revoking:
```graphql
mutation RevokePasskey($passkeyId: ID!) {
    revokePasskey(passkeyId: $passkeyId)
}
```

Check `schema.graphqls` for `JSON`, `UUID`, `Passkey`, `PasskeyRegistrationResult` types — may need to add scalar definitions.

## Step 3: Add Repository Methods

**File:** `app/src/main/java/pub/hackers/android/data/repository/HackersPubRepository.kt`

Add methods mirroring the existing `loginByUsername`/`completeLoginChallenge` pattern:
- `getPasskeyAuthenticationOptions(sessionId: String): Result<String>` — returns options JSON
- `loginByPasskey(sessionId: String, authenticationResponse: String): Result<Session>` — returns session
- `getPasskeyRegistrationOptions(accountId: String): Result<String>` — returns options JSON
- `verifyPasskeyRegistration(accountId: String, name: String, registrationResponse: String): Result<PasskeyRegistrationResult>`
- `revokePasskey(passkeyId: String): Result<String?>`

## Step 4: Create PasskeyManager

**New file:** `app/src/main/java/pub/hackers/android/data/auth/PasskeyManager.kt`

Wraps Android Credential Manager API:
```kotlin
@Singleton
class PasskeyManager @Inject constructor(
    @ApplicationContext private val context: Context
) {
    private val credentialManager = CredentialManager.create(context)

    suspend fun authenticate(optionsJson: String, activity: Activity): String {
        val request = GetCredentialRequest(listOf(
            GetPublicKeyCredentialOption(optionsJson)
        ))
        val result = credentialManager.getCredential(activity, request)
        val credential = result.credential as PublicKeyCredential
        return credential.authenticationResponseJson
    }

    suspend fun register(optionsJson: String, activity: Activity): String {
        val request = CreatePublicKeyCredentialRequest(optionsJson)
        val result = credentialManager.createCredential(activity, request)
        val credential = result as CreatePublicKeyCredentialResponse
        return credential.registrationResponseJson
    }
}
```

## Step 5: Update Sign-In Screen

**Files:**
- `app/src/main/java/pub/hackers/android/ui/screens/auth/SignInViewModel.kt`
- `app/src/main/java/pub/hackers/android/ui/screens/auth/SignInScreen.kt`

### ViewModel changes:
Add `signInWithPasskey(activity: Activity)`:
1. Generate UUID for `sessionId`
2. Call `repository.getPasskeyAuthenticationOptions(sessionId)`
3. Call `passkeyManager.authenticate(optionsJson, activity)`
4. Call `repository.loginByPasskey(sessionId, authenticationResponse)`
5. Save session via `sessionManager.saveSession(...)`

### Screen changes:
- Add "Sign in with passkey" button on the username step (before the username input or as an alternative)
- Button calls `viewModel.signInWithPasskey(activity)`
- Need to pass `Activity` context — use `LocalContext.current as Activity`

## Step 6: Add Passkey Management to Settings

**Files:**
- `app/src/main/java/pub/hackers/android/ui/screens/settings/SettingsViewModel.kt`
- `app/src/main/java/pub/hackers/android/ui/screens/settings/SettingsScreen.kt`

### ViewModel changes:
- Add `passkeys: List<Passkey>` to UI state
- `loadPasskeys()` — fetch via `account.passkeys` (need to add this to the viewer/account query)
- `registerPasskey(name: String, activity: Activity)` — call registration flow
- `revokePasskey(passkeyId: String)` — call revoke mutation

### Screen changes:
- Add "Passkeys" section when logged in
- List registered passkeys with name, created date, last used
- "Add passkey" button → dialog for name → registration flow
- Swipe/button to revoke passkey with confirmation

## Files to Modify

| File | Action |
|------|--------|
| `build.gradle.kts` | Add Credential Manager dependencies |
| `operations.graphql` | Add 5 passkey mutations |
| `schema.graphqls` | Verify JSON/Passkey types exist |
| `HackersPubRepository.kt` | Add 5 passkey repository methods |
| `data/auth/PasskeyManager.kt` | **New** — Credential Manager wrapper |
| `SignInViewModel.kt` | Add `signInWithPasskey()` |
| `SignInScreen.kt` | Add passkey button on login screen |
| `SettingsViewModel.kt` | Add passkey list/register/revoke |
| `SettingsScreen.kt` | Add passkey management UI |

## Verification

1. Build succeeds
2. Sign-in screen shows "Sign in with passkey" button
3. Tapping passkey button → system biometric prompt → login succeeds
4. Settings shows registered passkeys
5. Can add new passkey from settings
6. Can revoke passkey from settings
7. Test with `adb shell am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d "https://hackers.pub/@username"` to verify assetlinks still works (needed for `get_login_creds` relation)

Result.success(response.data?.revokePasskey)\n            }\n        } catch (e: Exception) {\n            Result.failure(e)\n        }\n    }\n\n    suspend fun createNote(\n        content: String,\n        language: String = \"en\",\n        visibility: PostVisibility = PostVisibility.PUBLIC,"

  "new_string": "    fun clearError() {\n        _uiState.update { it.copy(error = null) }\n    }\n\n    private fun jsonToMap(json: org.json.JSONObject): Map<String, Any?> {\n        val map = mutableMapOf<String, Any?>()\n        val keys = json.keys()\n        while (keys.hasNext()) {\n            val key = keys.next()\n            val value = json.get(key)\n            map[key] = when (value) {\n                is org.json.JSONObject -> jsonToMap(value)\n                is org.json.JSONArray -> jsonToList(value)\n                org.json.JSONObject.NULL -> null\n                else -> value\n            }\n        }\n        return map\n    }\n\n    private fun jsonToList(array: org.json.JSONArray): List<Any?> {\n        return (0 until array.length()).map { i ->\n            when (val value = array.get(i)) {\n                is org.json.JSONObject -> jsonToMap(value)\n                is org.json.JSONArray -> jsonToList(value)\n                org.json.JSONObject.NULL -> null\n                else -> value\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}"
}

157	    private fun getDirSize(dir: java.io.File): Long {

172	            else -> String.format("%.1f GB", bytes / (1024.0 * 1024 * 1024))
173	        }

it.copy(isLoadingPasskeys = true) }\n            repository.getPasskeys()\n                .onSuccess { result ->\n                    _uiState.update {\n                        it.copy(\n                            passkeys = result.passkeys,\n                            accountId = result.accountId,\n                            isLoadingPasskeys = false\n                        )\n                    }\n                }\n                .onFailure {\n                    _uiState.update { it.copy(isLoadingPasskeys = false) }\n                }\n        }\n    }\n\n    fun registerPasskey(name: String, activity: Activity) {\n        val accountId = _uiState.value.accountId ?: return\n        viewModelScope.launch {\n            _uiState.update { it.copy(isRegisteringPasskey = true) }\n            try {\n                val optionsJson = repository.getPasskeyRegistrationOptions(accountId)\n                    .getOrThrow()\n\n                val registrationResponse = passkeyManager.register(optionsJson, activity)\n                val responseMap = jsonToMap(org.json.JSONObject(registrationResponse))\n\n                val result = repository.verifyPasskeyRegistration(accountId, name, responseMap)\n                    .getOrThrow()\n\n                if (result.verified) {\n                    _uiState.update {\n                        it.copy(\n                            message = \"Passkey registered\",\n                            isRegisteringPasskey = false\n                        )\n                    }\n                    loadPasskeys()\n                } else {\n                    _uiState.update {\n                        it.copy(\n                            message = \"Passkey registration failed\",\n                            isRegisteringPasskey = false\n                        )\n                    }\n                }\n            } catch (e: Exception) {\n                _uiState.update {\n                    it.copy(\n                        message = e.message ?: \"Passkey registration failed\",\n                        isRegisteringPasskey = false\n                    )\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    fun revokePasskey(passkeyId: String) {\n        viewModelScope.launch {\n            repository.revokePasskey(passkeyId)\n                .onSuccess {\n                    _uiState.update { state ->\n                        state.copy(\n                            passkeys = state.passkeys.filter { it.id != passkeyId },\n                            message = \"Passkey removed\"\n                        )\n                    }\n                }\n                .onFailure {\n                    _uiState.update { it.copy(message = \"Failed to remove passkey\") }\n                }\n        }\n    }\n\n    private fun jsonToMap(json: org.json.JSONObject): Map<String, Any?> {\n        val map = mutableMapOf<String, Any?>()\n        val keys = json.keys()\n        while (keys.hasNext()) {\n            val key = keys.next()\n            val value = json.get(key)\n            map[key] = when (value) {\n                is org.json.JSONObject -> jsonToMap(value)\n                is org.json.JSONArray -> jsonToList(value)\n                org.json.JSONObject.NULL -> null\n                else -> value\n            }\n        }\n        return map\n    }\n\n    private fun jsonToList(array: org.json.JSONArray): List<Any?> {\n        return (0 until array.length()).map { i ->\n            when (val value = array.get(i)) {\n                is org.json.JSONObject -> jsonToMap(value)\n                is org.json.JSONArray -> jsonToList(value)\n                org.json.JSONObject.NULL -> null\n                else -> value\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}"

```bash
./gradlew installDebug
```

Then try again with:

```

> DEVELOPER

Okay, the log has not spawned. Is it passkey provider problem?

> AGENT

The `CredManProvService: Create Result` line IS from the Credential Manager — it returned a result but no `PasskeyAuth` log appeared. Either the new build wasn't installed, or the app restarted with a new PID.

Try this all-in-one:

```bash
./gradlew installDebug && adb logcat -c && adb logcat -s PasskeyAuth:D AndroidRuntime:E
```

Then tap the passkey button. If still nothing, try without the filter:

```bash
adb logcat --pid=$(adb shell pidof pub.hackers.android.dev) | grep -i "passkey\|error\|exception"
```

> DEVELOPER

Is it the callback problem?

> AGENT

Yes, likely. The `CredManProvService: Create Result returned from framework:` shows the passkey prompt completed, but the result isn't reaching your app's callback. This is a known issue on Samsung devices — the Credential Manager callback can get lost when the activity lifecycle changes.

The fix: use `PendingGetCredentialRequest` or ensure the activity isn't being recreated. But first, let me check if the issue is simpler — the Credential Manager might be throwing an exception that's being silently swallowed.

Found it. Line 64: `expectedOrigin: new URL(origin).origin` — the server expects `https://hackers.pub` as the origin, but Android's Credential Manager sends `android:apk-key-hash:<hash>` as the origin in `clientDataJSON`.

This is a **server-side issue**. The server needs to also accept the Android app's origin. The `@simplewebauthn/server` library's `verifyRegistrationResponse` accepts an array of origins:

```typescript
expectedOrigin: [new URL(origin).origin, "android:apk-key-hash:..."]
```

This needs to be fixed in the hackerspub server project. The Android app is sending the correct data — the server just doesn't accept the Android origin.

Want me to fix this in the server project (`models/passkey.ts`)?

> DEVELOPER

Is this right?

> AGENT

Yes, this is correct. The server at line 64 checks:

```typescript
expectedOrigin: new URL(origin).origin,  // "https://hackers.pub"
```

But Android's Credential Manager sends a different origin in `clientDataJSON`. When `assetlinks.json` is properly set up with `get_login_creds` and the package/fingerprint match, the origin should be `https://hackers.pub`. But your debug build uses `pub.hackers.android.dev` which doesn't match `pub.hackers.android` in `assetlinks.json`, so the Credential Manager falls back to `android:apk-key-hash:<hash>`.

Two fixes:

1. **Quick (for testing)**: Add the Android origin to the server's expected origins
2. **Proper (for production)**: The production app (`pub.hackers.android`) with matching fingerprint will use `https://hackers.pub` as origin automatically — no server change needed

Want to test with the release build first to confirm it works without server changes?

> AGENT

Same error from the release build. The issue is server-side — "Unexpected error" is a generic catch-all from the GraphQL resolver. It's not an origin mismatch (that would be a specific error from `@simplewebauthn`).

The most likely cause: the `registrationResponse` JSON structure isn't matching what `@simplewebauthn/server`'s `verifyRegistrationResponse` expects. Apollo might be serializing the `Map` differently than raw JSON.

This needs a server-side fix to see the actual error. Can you check the server logs for the error at `15:35:52`? The server should have a stack trace showing what exactly failed in `verifyRegistrationResponse`.

> DEVELOPER

Okay, android-apk-hash is it consistent for all versions?

> AGENT

No. The `android:apk-key-hash` is derived from the **signing key**, not the APK itself. So:

- Same signing key = same hash across all versions
- Different signing key = different hash

Since you always sign releases with the same keystore (`hackerspub-release.jks`), the hash is consistent across all app versions. It only changes if you change the signing key.

> AGENT

The key is `"${it.id}_${it.sharedPost?.id.orEmpty()}"`. If the same note appears twice in the timeline (e.g., directly AND as someone's repost), and both have no `sharedPost`, they'd produce the same key like `"NoteId_"`.

Fix: add the index to guarantee uniqueness.

> TOOL

tool_use Edit
id: toolu_01PYtG4bPXm2Cp7pE4N4myno
```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/kodingwarrior/fediverse/hackerspub-android/app/src/main/java/pub/hackers/android/ui/screens/timeline/TimelineScreen.kt",
  "old_string": "                                key = { \"${it.id}_${it.sharedPost?.id.orEmpty()}\" }",
  "new_string": "                                key = { post -> \"${post.id}_${post.sharedPost?.id.orEmpty()}_${uiState.posts.indexOf(post)}\" }"
}
```

> AGENT

Still duplicates — the `distinctBy { it.id }` isn't enough because a repost has the same `it.id` as the original post (the wrapper post ID). The real issue is that the API returns two entries with different wrapper posts but the same underlying `sharedPost.id`, and since we use the wrapper `it.id`, they can still clash.

The problem is actually that `loadMore` appends posts that may overlap with existing ones. Let me also deduplicate in the ViewModel when appending:

> AGENT

Now deduplication happens at three levels:
1. **Repository** — `distinctBy { it.id }` on initial fetch
2. **ViewModel loadMore** — `distinctBy { p -> p.id }` when appending pages
3. **LazyColumn** — simple `key = { it.id }` (safe since duplicates are eliminated)

Done. All passkey UI is gated behind `FeatureFlags.PASSKEY_AUTH_ENABLED = false`:

- **Sign-in screen**: passkey button hidden when flag is `false`
- **Settings screen**: passkey section, add dialog, and revoke dialog all hidden
- **Data layer**: code stays intact, just not called from UI

To enable later, just flip to `true` in `FeatureFlags.kt`.
